clue.text: Put together our clothes, prepared to sign up

parts.note: to join things is to put them together

indicators.note: the letters of our clothes are prepared, i.e. worked up into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone assembles a group's uniforms, ready to enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: To join the colours is to enlist in the army; the colours are a regiment's flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining the colours is the idiom for enlisting as a soldier, which is signing up.

clue.text: Compiler in trousers: are you about to become intellectual?

indicators.note: the compiler's name sits in the trousers, between the last two letters

parts.note: jeans are a kind of trousers
Paul is a fellow Guardian crossword setter (compiler)
'thou art' is the archaic form of 'you are'
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A setter in jeans is asked whether they are turning highbrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Compiler here means crossword setter: Paul is another Guardian setter's pseudonym. ART is the old second-person form of 'are', as in 'thou art'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French existentialist philosopher is a famous example of an intellectual.

clue.text: Sort of faith I will take lots of tricks, diamonds mostly

parts.note: taken as written
in bridge a slam is winning all or nearly all the tricks

indicators.note: only most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player boasts of winning heaps of tricks, chiefly in diamonds, as an article of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: A slam in bridge means taking all (grand) or all but one (small) of the tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic describes a particular religion, so it names one sort of faith in adjectival use.

clue.text: Short-lived rain's poured in many a time

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go inside the word for many a time, after its first letter

parts.note: TEN T, read playfully as ten times (T for time)

indicators.note: rain that has poured is rearranged, its letters running into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something brief, though rain has bucketed down over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN T reads as 'ten times', with T the abbreviation for time: a fair stand-in for many a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transient passes quickly, a direct synonym for brief or fleeting in duration.

clue.text: Old legal right in French is superior

parts.note: est is French for 'is'
over means above, in a superior position

explanation.surface: A historic entitlement in French law is ranked higher than others.
explanation.walkthrough: An estover was a tenant's right to take wood from the land for fuel or repairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Estover is an archaic term in property law for a tenant's entitlement to gather timber.

clue.text: Bound to make line break important in dictionary

indicators.note: the built-up piece is placed inside the dictionary abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: the line breaks into the word for important, splitting it

parts.note: big means important, as in a big decision

explanation.surface: A lexicographer feels compelled to insert a line break into a major entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obliged to do something means being bound or compelled to do it.

clue.text: Master reacts offensively principally falling over rootstock

indicators.note: a down light falling over is turned upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: sir is a respectful form of address, like master

indicators.note: only the principal, leading letters of these words are used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher lashes out and topples onto a plant's base.
explanation.walkthrough: Orris root, from irises, is used in perfumery.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is the fragrant rhizome of certain irises, so it is literally a rootstock.

clue.text: Stalks over the floor in a hurry, cutting friend short

parts.note: a rush is a hurry

indicators.note: the friend is cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: mate is British informal for friend

explanation.surface: Someone strides hurriedly across the room, curtly snubbing a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalks' looks like a verb of walking, but it means plant stems spread on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor covering woven from rush stems is literally plant stalks laid on the ground.

clue.text: Callas's able somehow to retain musical sense with purest tone

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the sense inside them
the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: taken as written
a good ear is a sense of musical pitch

explanation.surface: Maria Callas, the opera diva, could somehow keep her musical feel while singing pure notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile describes a sound that is perfectly clean and ringing, like a struck bell, hence pure in tone.

clue.text: Finally securing a little energy: that's something

indicators.note: the outer phrase secures, or holds, the extra letter inside it

parts.note: at last means finally
E is the symbol for energy, a single letter

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets a small boost of energy and takes comfort in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as consolation, 'at least' carries the sense of 'well, that is some small comfort'.

clue.text: See increases in slow slender creatures

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
rises means increases

explanation.surface: Watch how the sluggish, thin animals grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lorises are small nocturnal primates; the slow and slender species are named for exactly those traits.

clue.text: Alcohol? A tiny taste, about two months back

indicators.note: the whole is put back to front
the taste goes about, surrounding, the two months

parts.note: a sip is a tiny taste of a drink
M is the abbreviation for month, twice

explanation.surface: Someone recalls only a small sample of booze a couple of months ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Pimm's is a gin-based British summer drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pimm's is a brand of gin-based liqueur, so it is one example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Gives mail out, based on a score

indicators.note: the letters are sent out of their order, as the post goes out

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A postal worker hands out letters according to a tally.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigesimal means counting in twenties, and a score is twenty.

clue.text: Waiting for security pass, as Stalin's nephew might have said?

indicators.note: introduces the imagined speaker whose words are heard
spoken words point to a sound-alike of what is entered

parts.note: a nephew of Stalin might call him Uncle Red, Stalin being a Communist

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck awaiting clearance, which a Soviet relative might phrase oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour of Communism, so a nephew of Stalin could address him as 'Uncle Red'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet cleared by security is still waiting for approval or a pass.

clue.text: Prime ministers given a flatbread

parts.note: both William Pitt the Elder and the Younger were British Prime Ministers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Political leaders are served a piece of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The name covers two Prime Ministers, father and son.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a Middle Eastern bread baked flat, a kind of flatbread.

clue.text: Stop admitting a latitude that's commonly accepted

indicators.note: the outer word admits, lets in, the other letters

parts.note: to prevent is to stop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A refusal to allow leeway becomes the general view.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread, generally found or held by most people.

clue.text: A great deal expected soon in this

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 'a ...' as in 'a ... better', i.e. a great deal

explanation.walkthrough: The answer works with 'a' (a sight more) and with 'in' (the end is in sight).
explanation.definitionFit: Informally 'a sight' means a lot, and anything in view is near at hand, so coming soon.

clue.text: One morbidly interested in death, say, remains in a stew

indicators.note: say signals that the word is only heard, not spelt

parts.note: a ghoul is someone with a morbid interest in death
ash is what remains after cremation

explanation.surface: A death-obsessed person's remains end up in a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a stew' suggests being agitated, but the stew is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Goulash is a Hungarian meat dish cooked slowly in liquid, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Result of overindulgence perhaps troubling, Pepys said

indicators.note: the letters are troubled, stirred up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The diarist Samuel Pepys complains of a disturbing outcome of too much feasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, which eating or drinking too much may cause.

clue.text: Tricky position, lying on front between two women

indicators.note: the letter sits between the two names

parts.note: Di and Emma, two women's names

indicators.note: only the front letter of the word is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lies face down between two women, which is awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult situation with no good way out, a tricky predicament.

clue.text: Always in black, which is OK for a speaker

indicators.note: the word for always goes in the word for black

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry
ay (aye) is an old word for always

explanation.surface: Always dressing in black is acceptable for a public speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sayable can be said without offence, so it is fine for someone talking to utter.

clue.text: One doesn't believe it's cold through the month, almost freezing!

indicators.note: the cold letter goes through the month, within it

parts.note: Sept is the short form of September

indicators.note: not quite all the word, its last letter missing

parts.note: ice is freezing cold

explanation.surface: A doubter insists that it is chilly all month and near freezing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is a doubter, someone who questions or does not accept claims.

clue.text: Simple song: could it be any louder?

indicators.note: asks whether the letters could be something else, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A listener asks whether a plain tune can be turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundelay is a short simple song with a refrain, an old lyrical form.

clue.text: Cyclist has her day in the lead, weather having improved

indicators.note: the rider gets her letter moved; joins with in the lead
puts the letter at the front, ahead of the rest, as a leader in a race

parts.note: a rider is someone on a bike
D is the abbreviation for day, here the rider's own

explanation.surface: A cyclist finally wins a stage once the rain clears.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDER's D, 'her day', comes out of fourth place and goes 'in the lead', at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: When the weather improves after rain, conditions become less wet, so it is drier.

clue.text: Competitive place a long time back

indicators.note: the phrase is read back to front

parts.note: an era is a long time

explanation.surface: A sporting venue from ages ago.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue where contests are held, a place for competition.

clue.text: Artistic style of boxer's, with rapid movement around

indicators.note: the sleep phase goes around the boxer's name

parts.note: REM is rapid eye movement
Muhammad Ali, the boxer, with the possessive

explanation.surface: A boxer's art form involves fast footwork all round.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is an art movement that depicts subjects truthfully, as they really are.

clue.text: Whisper, about to go in to get clean

indicators.note: the short word is set to go in the longer one

parts.note: to bathe is to wash, to get clean
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Someone murmurs about stepping into the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe a word is to utter it softly, so whisper as a verb.

clue.text: A peculiar match abandoned with reference to drugs

indicators.note: the letters are abandoned to disorder, wildly rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd game is called off, perhaps over a doping scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmaceutical describes medicinal drugs and their preparation.
